title: Flyto2 Core sibling modules -- T1190 numerous HTTP-emitting modules carry an inert SSRF metadata tag and call no guard at all
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-67428 (GHSA-pgwh-4jj4-qm8v,
CVSS 8.5 HIGH), affecting Flyto2 Core (`flyto-core`) <= 2.26.6.

Flyto2's SSRF guard (`validate_url_with_env_config`) is per-module
with no global egress interception, and a wide set of HTTP-emitting
modules -- `core.api.http_get`, `core.api.http_post`,
`graphql.query`/`graphql.mutation`, `monitor.http_check`,
`communication.slack_send`, the `discord`/`slack`/`teams`
notification senders, the `ai.vision_analyze` Anthropic path,
`verify.visual_diff`, `browser.proxy_rotate`, and the `agent`/`llm`
inline `base_url` branch -- never call it. Each carries only an
`ssrf_protected` metadata tag string that enforces nothing; a repo
grep of the exemplar module for `validate_url`/`ssrf`/`is_private`
returns zero guard calls. An authenticated workflow-author can point
any of these modules' URL parameter directly at the cloud metadata IP
or an internal host and receive the full response body back, with no
encoding trick required.

Detection logic flags an invocation of one of this advisory's named
unguarded modules whose URL parameter targets the cloud metadata
address or a private/loopback range -- the exact direct-IP SSRF this
advisory's live proof of concept confirms, contrasted against the
guarded sibling `http.get` rejecting the identical input on the same
instance.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (flyto-core, via
GHSA and NVD, citing every affected module by name, the exact source
file with zero guard-call hits, and a live proof of concept
contrasting guarded vs. unguarded behavior on identical input), fixed in flyto-core 2.26.7+ (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
